examples.en: The weather has suddenly gotten quite chilly lately.
I haven't been sleeping well lately.

examples.ko: 요사이 회사 일이 많아서 정신이 없어요.
examples.en: I have so much work these days that I'm swamped.
I haven't heard anything from my friends lately.

explain: '요즘', '요새'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. '요새'는 '요사이'를 줄인 말이에요. 문장 맨 앞에서 '요사이 어때요?'처럼 안부를 물을 때도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: What have you been up to these days?
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common word for this meaning.

phrases.en: I've been tired lately because I have a lot of work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '요사이'를 줄인 말로 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 'yosai', common in conversation.

phrases.en: Long time no see. How are you these days?
phrases.nuance_ko: 안부를 물을 때 문장 앞에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used at the start of a sentence to ask how someone is.

explain_en: It means almost the same as '요즘' and '요새'; '요새' is the contracted form of '요사이'. You can put it at the start of a sentence to ask how someone is, as in '요사이 어때요?'.

t90.ax: I haven't been sleeping well lately.

examples.en: I looked for the information I needed on the web.

examples.ko: 이 웹 사이트는 한국어로도 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can view this website in Korean too.

examples.ko: 웹 디자인을 배우고 싶어서 학원에 등록했어요.
examples.en: I wanted to learn web design, so I signed up at an academy.

examples.ko: 제 친구는 웹 개발자로 일하고 있어요.
examples.en: My friend works as a web developer.

examples.ko: 집에서 웹으로 예약하면 훨씬 더 싸요.
examples.en: It's much cheaper if you book on the web from home.

examples.ko: 동생은 웹 소설을 읽느라 밤을 새웠어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling stayed up all night reading web novels.

explain: '웹'은 보통 다른 말 앞에 붙어서 '웹 사이트', '웹툰', '웹 소설'처럼 써요. 그냥 '인터넷'이라고 해도 되지만, 인터넷 페이지를 말할 때는 '웹'이 자주 나와요. 한국에서는 '웹툰'을 많이 봐요.

phrases.en: I check the timetable on the school website.
phrases.nuance_ko: '웹' 뒤에 붙어 인터넷 페이지를 말해요. 줄여서 '사이트'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 웹 attached to 사이트 refers to an internet page; people also just say 사이트.

phrases.en: I read webtoons on the subway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인터넷으로 보는 한국식 만화예요. 한국에서 아주 인기가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Korean-style comics read online; very popular in Korea.

phrases.en: I study Korean while reading web novels.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인터넷에서 연재하는 소설이에요. 종이책과 달리 휴대폰으로 읽어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A novel published online in installments, read on a phone rather than on paper.

explain_en: 웹 usually attaches to another word, as in 웹 사이트, 웹툰, and 웹 소설. You could just say 인터넷, but 웹 comes up often when talking about internet pages. Webtoons (웹툰) are very popular in Korea.

examples.en: Every morning the garbage truck passes through our neighborhood.
The garbage truck's noise startled me awake.
The garbage truck usually comes early in the morning.

examples.ko: 아이들이 청소차를 보면 신나서 손을 흔들어요.
examples.en: When children see the garbage truck, they wave excitedly.
The road is narrow, so even the garbage truck can't get in.

explain: '쓰레기차'라고도 말해요. 쓰레기를 모아 가는 차라서 '쓰레기를 싣다', '쓰레기를 수거하다'와 같이 나와요. 소방차, 구급차처럼 '-차' 이름의 특수한 차 중 하나예요.

phrases.en: A garbage truck is parked in the alley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy synonym with the same meaning.

phrases.en: Put out the trash before the garbage truck comes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓰레기를 가져가는 시간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about trash pickup time.

phrases.en: I said hello to the garbage truck driver.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청소차를 운전하는 분을 높여 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to refer to the truck's driver.

explain_en: People also say '쓰레기차'. Since it collects trash, it appears with '쓰레기를 싣다' (load) and '쓰레기를 수거하다' (collect). It's one of the special vehicles with '-차' names, like '소방차' and '구급차'.

examples.en: I have one older brother.
My older brother is three years older than me.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 친형과 같은 방을 썼어요.
examples.en: Since I was little, I shared a room with my older brother.

examples.ko: 친형 때문에 저도 축구를 좋아하게 됐어요.
examples.en: Because of my older brother, I came to like soccer too.
I borrowed my older brother's phone and made a call.

explain: 남자가 자기 형을 말할 때 '형'이라고 해요. 사촌 형이나 친한 동네 형이 아니라 진짜 형제라고 분명히 하고 싶을 때 '친형'이라고 해요. 여자의 오빠는 '친오빠', 언니는 '친언니'예요.

phrases.en: I have one older brother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 보통 '형'이라고만 해요. '친형'은 진짜 형제라고 분명히 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life people just say 'hyeong'. 'Chinhyeong' stresses a real brother.

phrases.en: My older brother works at a company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람에게 높여 말할 때 '님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'nim' makes it more respectful when speaking to others.

phrases.en: We are not cousins; we are real brothers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사촌이 아니라 같은 부모의 형제라고 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to make clear that you are brothers with the same parents, not cousins.

explain_en: Blood-related older brother, as opposed to a cousin or older male friend. A man calls his older brother 형. Say 친형 when you want to make clear it is your real brother, not a cousin or a friendly older guy from the neighborhood. A woman says 친오빠 or 친언니.

examples.en: I wrote the appointment in my phone calendar.

examples.ko: 캘린더 앱에 친구 생일을 모두 저장했어요.
examples.en: I saved all my friends' birthdays in the calendar app.
Looking at the calendar, next week is a holiday.

examples.ko: 이 캘린더는 한국 공휴일이 다 나와 있어요.
examples.en: This calendar shows all the Korean public holidays.
Tomorrow's meeting time changed in the calendar.
I made a shared calendar with my friend.

explain: 한국에서는 종이 달력은 '달력'을 더 많이 쓰고, 휴대폰 앱이나 컴퓨터 일정표에는 '캘린더'를 많이 써요. 같은 사물이지만 말하는 장면이 조금 달라요. '캘린더에 넣다', '캘린더 공유'처럼 앱 이야기에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: I put the appointment in my calendar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일정을 앱에 저장할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for saving an event in a calendar app.

phrases.en: I manage my schedule with a calendar app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰의 일정 앱을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the schedule app on a phone.

phrases.example: 친구와 캘린더 공유를 해서 약속 잡기가 쉬워요.
phrases.en: Sharing calendars with my friend makes planning easy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일정을 다른 사람과 같이 볼 수 있게 하는 것이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Letting others see your schedule too.

explain_en: Loanword, often a phone app, planner, or trendy designed calendar. For a paper calendar Koreans prefer 달력, while 캘린더 is more common for phone apps and computer schedules. 캘린더에 넣다 and 캘린더 공유 often come up when talking about apps.

t90.ax: I made a shared calendar with my friend.

examples.en: At the zoo, a panda is eating bamboo.
I bought one panda doll.
A baby panda was born and it was on the news.
Pandas eat and sleep all day.

examples.ko: 친구는 판다를 보러 중국에 가고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: My friend wants to go to China to see pandas.

explain: 한국에서도 판다는 아주 인기 있는 동물이라 '푸바오'처럼 이름이 붙은 판다 이야기가 뉴스에 자주 나와요. 판다는 곰과 비슷해서 '판다 곰'이라고도 하지만 보통 그냥 판다라고 말해요.

phrases.en: The baby panda is really cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어린 판다를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a young panda.

phrases.example: 판다 곰은 하루 종일 대나무를 먹어요.
phrases.en: Pandas eat bamboo all day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곰과 비슷해서 붙인 말이지만 보통은 '판다'라고만 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Mentions the bear resemblance, but people usually just say 판다.

phrases.en: I gave my younger sibling a panda doll.
phrases.nuance_ko: 판다 모양의 인형을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A stuffed toy shaped like a panda.

explain_en: Pandas are hugely popular in Korea, and named pandas like 푸바오 often make the news. They're bear-like, so 판다 곰 also exists, but people usually just say 판다.

examples.en: I was startled when a phone call suddenly came in the middle of the night.
The baby woke up and cried in the middle of the night.

explain: 밤이 가장 깊은 때를 말하고, '한밤중'이라고도 해요. 늦은 저녁이나 새벽보다 더 깊은 밤 느낌이라 '한밤에 전화하다'처럼 놀랍거나 예의에 어긋나는 일과 같이 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: It rained a lot in the middle of the night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '한밤'과 거의 같고, 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 한밤, and more common in daily speech.

phrases.en: I had a scary dream and woke up in the middle of the night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깊은 밤에 잠에서 깰 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when waking up in the deep of night.
phrases.en_equiv: to wake up in the middle of the night

phrases.en: The street in the middle of the night is very quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깊은 밤의 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a scene in the deep of night.

explain_en: It refers to the deepest part of the night and is also said as '한밤중'. It feels deeper than late evening or dawn, so it often appears with surprising or impolite things, like calling someone in the middle of the night.

t90.ax: The baby woke up and cried in the middle of the night.

examples.en: Phew, the exam is finally over.
Phew, luckily I didn't miss the train.
Phew, today was a really hard day.

examples.ko: 휴, 이번 달 월급이 벌써 다 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: Sigh, this month's pay is already gone.

examples.ko: 휴, 이제 겨우 숙제를 다 했어요.
examples.en: Phew, I've only just finished my homework.

explain: 한숨을 쉬듯 내는 소리로, 안심했을 때와 힘들거나 걱정될 때 둘 다 써요. 소리가 같아서 상황과 표정으로 구분해요. 문자나 메신저에서는 '휴…'처럼 점을 붙여 쓰고, 쉬는 날을 뜻하는 '휴가'의 '휴'와는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: Phew, today was really hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '휴'와 비슷하지만 힘들거나 지칠 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '휴', but used more often when tired or worn out.

phrases.en: Phew, I just barely arrived on time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '휴'보다 숨을 길게 내쉬는 느낌이고 안심했을 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A longer exhale than '휴', often used when relieved.

phrases.en: Phew, I finished all my homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: '휴'를 길게 늘인 말로 한숨을 더 크게 쉬는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A drawn-out '휴' that sounds like a bigger sigh.

explain_en: A sound like letting out a breath, used both for relief and for fatigue or worry. Since the sound is the same, context and facial expression tell them apart. In texts it is often written with dots, as in '휴…', and it is unrelated to the '휴' in '휴가' (vacation).

t90.ax: Phew, the exam is finally over.
